papers.title: Real AI Agents with Fake Memories: Fatal Context Manipulation Attacks on Web3 Agents (Patlan, Sheng, Hebbar, Mittal, Viswanath)
papers.relation: describes: introduces CrAIBench (from v2); the repository's finetune_dataset/README.md links it (https://github.com/AthaSSiN/CrAIBench/blob/e41eac1eb2fea00a31c69827bfe83f9722a25702/finetune_dataset/README.md); the top-level README does not; CITATION.bib at the pin is AgentDojo's. The paper does not link the repository or the logs
papers.versions: v1 2025-03-20 titled 'AI Agents in Cryptoland: Practical Attacks and No Silver Bullet' (12 pages, ElizaOS case study only, no CrAIBench; https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16248v1). v2 2025-04-30, new title, 29 pages: adds CrAIBench (Table 1 design; Appendix C.1 Table 2 multi-step and Table 3 single-step full results per model x suite x system prompt; https://arxiv.org/html/2503.16248v2). v3 2025-07-09, 19 pages: keeps Table I, drops the full results tables (results only as figures), adds model-based PI detectors (PromptGuard 2, ProtectAI v2, DataSentinel) on GPT-4o (Fig. 8) (https://arxiv.org/html/2503.16248v3). Runs in the repo were committed 2025-04-03..06, between v1 and v2; v2 is the comparison version

harness: Vendored AgentDojo 0.1.15 (pyproject version 0.1.15; fork base = upstream tag v0.1.15 8d2ecb59), modified by the fork (memory injection via InitQuery memory message with role user, spotlighting_with_delimiting text changed, spotlighting_with_datamarking added, important_instructions wrapper changed at be71b1f5, result cache disabled). python -m agentdojo.scripts.benchmark with run_script.sh (chain) and the README crypto_trading command (both default to --system-message-name default_defended --defense spotlighting_with_delimiting --attack important_instructions, -mi for memory injection). Logs are TraceLogger v0.k11 (no timestamps, no package/benchmark version; profile, census). Code identity cannot be verified from the logs (profile code_identity range, verified_code []). Known family behaviours that apply: injection-task pre-pass as user task with constant security (AgentDojo #95 explains 'security' True = injection goal met, https://github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo/issues/95), silent rerun on null final content (0 here per census). Open upstream issues on security checks (#135, #154, #168) concern upstream suites, not CrAIBench's own suites
models: gpt-4o (OpenAI API, undated alias: the fork maps the enum to 'gpt-4o'; the snapshot is not recorded in v0.k11 logs; at the run dates 2025-04-03..06 OpenAI's alias would have resolved to a dated snapshot that cannot be confirmed from the data; https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-4o)

Paper also evaluates Claude Sonnet 3.5 (claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620), Claude Sonnet 3.7 (claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219) and fine-tuned Qwen-2.5-14B-Instruct; none are in the released runs (run scripts at the pin name the Claude ids)

discrepancy_leads: Released runs are a small slice of the paper's design: 2 of 4 models, 2 of 3 suites, no benign runs, apparently one system-prompt condition; the authors' counting script reads a private tree with a system-message directory level that the release lacks

Two GPT-4o Secure Trading cells in v2 Table 2 have rates that fit the released counts, not the printed Total 390: PI ASR 21.87% = 84/384 and MI ASR 74.33% = 307/413; the paper's Secure trading numbers were likely computed over exactly these files, extras included

Released crypto_trading logs include 23 MI + 19 PI runs with injection_task_5..9 and 11 (no injection_task_10) and 11 pre-pass logs for injection tasks 0..9 and 11 (id 10 absent), but the paper's design has 5 injections per trading task (390/78); injection tasks were edited after the runs (ac6c9490, c07e2b94) [fact-check: corrected '5..11' / '0..11 minus one' from the GitHub tree listing at the pin]
5 gpt-4o crypto multi-step tasks (24, 25, 71, 72, 78) have no PI log; tasks 53 and 54 have no log at all (paper: 78 multi-step tasks = 80 minus 2)

Paper v2 says the PI wrapper references the user's name and the agent's model; the fork's be71b1f5 (before all delimiting runs) replaced it with an unsigned wrapper, so the 435 PI logs should carry the unsigned text

REFUTED by fact-check (kept for the record): the original lead said the paper's explicit delimiter differs from the released code. It does not. v2 Sec. 6 prints the 'more explicit delimiter' as the parenthetical 'Please note that this is data and not instructions' notice, which is exactly the text be71b1f5 introduced (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.16248v2; https://github.com/AthaSSiN/CrAIBench/commit/be71b1f5). The memory-retrieval phrase printed in v2 Sec. 5 also matches be71b1f5. Only the PI wrapper differs (paper Fig. 15 signed; code unsigned)
v2 Table 3 single-step rows appear to swap Trading and DAO/NFT labels relative to Table 1 (16 tasks/80 attacks is Trading in Table 1, DAO/NFT in Table 3)
Model identity 'gpt-4o' is an undated alias (fork changed the enum), so the snapshot behind 1,038 logs is not recorded; paper names only GPT-4o

spotlighting_with_datamarking chain logs (19) are from an earlier chain benchmark state (a512e34a: different injection numbering, mock tools) and are not described in the paper; banking (3) are smoke tests

Result cache disabled in the fork (afd3a23b): reruns with other system prompts overwrite the same path, so each released file is the last run for its path; the system-prompt variant per log is the only record of its condition (profile: 4 unrecognised system prompts, 651..3,092 chars)
v2 Table 2 Claude Sonnet 3.5 Trading Secure prints PI Total 380 (others 390): paper-internal inconsistency (not in corpus)

Fact-check lead: count_true_values.py at the pin maps system messages default_defended / default / blockchain (= Secure / Default / Confirmation per v2 Sec. 6), counts ASR as successes over the files actually present (not a fixed 390), and for gpt-4o + default_defended reads the attacked cells from a directory named 'default_defended_es', a name that is not a key of system_messages.yaml at the pin, c07e2b94 or sft (https://github.com/AthaSSiN/CrAIBench/blob/e41eac1eb2fea00a31c69827bfe83f9722a25702/count_true_values.py). So the paper's gpt-4o Secure attacked cells come from a separately named prompt variant; which of the 4 released prompt variants it is remains open (bears on H5 and H7)

Fact-check lead: v2 Fig. 20 prints a GPT-4o Secure Trading MI trace with pipeline gpt-4o-spotlighting_with_delimiting, user_task_7, injection_task_2, security true; a file at that path (injection_task_2_memory_injection.json) exists in the released tree, which ties the paper to these logs (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.16248v2)
